mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE is below 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of quarters with two consecutive declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically significantly higher than baseline during periods when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for three months indicates a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both > 2% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months and UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically significantly higher than baseline during periods of rapid, sustained payroll acceleration with stable unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between industrial production (INDPRO) and capacity utilization (not available, so use proxy: INDPRO and HOUST) over six months, with INDPRO rising while housing starts stagnate, signals supply-side bottlenecks, which raise costs and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rising while HOUST flat for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO rises and HOUST is flat for six months.
